problems.issue: The simulated cohort is 46% female despite PIGA-related MCAHS2 being an X-linked disorder predominantly affecting males. A nearly balanced sex distribution is implausible without explicit modeling of exceptional affected females.

Records inadequately represent the core developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, particularly hypotonia and severe developmental impairment. Clinically informative findings are also substantially underreported versus R1-train: cerebral visual impairment 4% versus 43%, callosal hypoplasia 9% versus 43%, and contractures 12% versus 50%.

Example records contain excessive unrelated or nonspecific findings. Short telomere length, verrucous papule, and progressive visual field defects in record 1 are not characteristic; record 2 lacks the defining neurological phenotype altogether. These records would teach misleading disease associations.

summary: The sex distribution and poorly represented neurological phenotype make these patients implausible. A median age of three years is compatible with this early-onset disorder.
